subject: General Aptitude
summary: syllogisms, if-then logic, number and letter series, coding, blood relations, directions, clocks and calendars, data sufficiency, seating arrangement, ranking and figure counting
next_day: Fluid Mechanics, Turbulent Flow & Pipe Losses

questions.text:
Statements: No engineer is lazy. All managers are engineers.
Conclusions: I. No manager is lazy. II. Some engineers are managers.
Which conclusion(s) follow(s)?
solution: Concept: Draw the Venn diagram: the managers circle lies inside the engineers circle, which is completely separate from the lazy circle.
I: managers sit inside engineers, so none of them can be lazy → follows. II: "All managers are engineers" converts to "Some engineers are managers" → follows.
Answer: both I and II.
Exam tip: "All A are B" converts only to "Some B are A", never to "All B are A".

questions.text: "The pump delivers water only if it is primed." The pump delivered water this morning. Which conclusion is certain?
opts: The pump was primed this morning
The pump was not primed this morning
A primed pump always delivers water
questions.ans: (A) The pump was primed this morning
solution: Concept: "P only if Q" means "if P then Q": delivery ⟹ primed.
The pump delivered water (P is true), so it was primed (Q is true).
Option (C) is the converse (Q ⟹ P), which is not implied.
Exam tip: "only if" introduces the necessary condition; "if" introduces the sufficient condition.

questions.text: The next term in the series 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ___ is ______
solution: Concept: Look at the differences: 4, 6, 8, 10, so the next difference is 12.
Exam tip: If first differences form an AP, the series is quadratic in n.

questions.text: Find the next letter in the series: B, E, I, N, ___
solution: Concept: Convert letters to positions: B = 2, E = 5, I = 9, N = 14.
Gaps are +3, +4, +5, so the next gap is +6: 14 + 6 = 20 = T.
Exam tip: Remember the EJOTY markers: E = 5, J = 10, O = 15, T = 20, Y = 25.

questions.text: In a certain code, GATE = 33 and MECH = 29. In the same code, PUMP = ______
solution: Concept: The code is the sum of the alphabet positions of the letters.
Exam tip: When a number code is given for a word, test the position sum, the product and the reverse positions (27 − n) first.

questions.text: A is B's brother. C is A's mother. D is C's father. How is A related to D?
solution: Concept: Build the family tree generation by generation.
D is C's father; C is A's mother, so D is A's maternal grandfather. A is male (a brother), so A is D's grandson.
Exam tip: Fix the gender of each person as soon as a word like brother, mother or father reveals it.

questions.text: A person walks 5 km east, turns left and walks 3 km, turns left again and walks 9 km, then turns left again and walks 6 km. His distance from the starting point (in km) is ______
solution: Concept: Track the coordinates (east = +x, north = +y).
East 5 → (5, 0); left = north 3 → (5, 3); left = west 9 → (−4, 3); left = south 6 → (−4, −3).
Distance = √(4² + 3²) = 5 km (towards the south-west).
Exam tip: Three left turns in a row bring you back to facing the original direction's right.

questions.text: The hands of a clock coincide for the first time after 3 o'clock at how many minutes past 3 (round off to two decimal places)? ______
solution: Concept: The minute hand gains 5.5° per minute on the hour hand.
At 3:00 the hour hand is 90° ahead. Time to close the gap = 90/5.5 = 180/11 min
Exam tip: The hands coincide 11 times in 12 hours, every 65 5/11 minutes.

questions.text: 1 January 2027 is a Friday. What day of the week is 1 March 2028?
solution: Concept: Count odd days (days beyond complete weeks).
1 Jan 2027 → 1 Jan 2028: 365 days = 1 odd day → Saturday.
1 Jan 2028 → 1 Mar 2028: January 31 + February 29 (2028 is a leap year) = 60 days = 4 odd days → Saturday + 4 = Wednesday.
Exam tip: A century year is a leap year only if divisible by 400; other years if divisible by 4.

questions.text:
Question: Is x > y, where x and y are real numbers?
Statement I: x² > y²
Statement II: x + y > 0
opts: Both statements together are sufficient, but neither alone is
Both statements together are not sufficient
questions.ans: (C) Both statements together are sufficient, but neither alone is
solution: Concept: Test each statement with counter-examples, then combine.
I alone: x = −3, y = 1 gives x² > y² but x < y; x = 3, y = 1 gives x > y. Not sufficient.
II alone: x = 1, y = 2 (no) and x = 2, y = 1 (yes). Not sufficient.
Together: x² − y² = (x − y)(x + y) > 0 with x + y > 0 forces x − y > 0. Both together are sufficient.
Exam tip: Factorising is often the fastest way to combine two inequality statements.

questions.text: Six friends A, B, C, D, E and F sit around a circular table facing the centre. A sits opposite D. B sits immediately to the right of A. C is not an immediate neighbour of D. E does not sit opposite B. Who sits opposite C?
solution: Concept: Fix A, then place the others clockwise (facing the centre, a person's right neighbour is the next seat anticlockwise).
Seats clockwise from A: A, 2, 3, D, 5, B (B is to A's right, D is opposite A).
C cannot be next to D (seats 3 and 5), so C = seat 2. E is not opposite B (seat 3), so E = seat 5 and F = seat 3.
Clockwise order: A, C, F, D, E, B. Opposite pairs: A–D, C–E, F–B. So E is opposite C.
Exam tip: In a circle facing the centre, left = clockwise and right = anticlockwise; facing outward, they swap.

questions.text: Ravi is 14th from the top and 27th from the bottom in his class. The number of students in the class is ______
solution: Concept: Total = rank from top + rank from bottom − 1 (Ravi is counted twice).
Exam tip: Between-two-people questions: number between = |difference of positions| − 1.

questions.text: The number of triangles in the figure shown is ______
solution: Concept: Every triangle here has its apex at the top vertex; its base is any segment between two of the four points on a horizontal line.
On the base line there are 4 points (the two corners and the two feet of the inner lines): C(4, 2) = 6 triangles.
On the middle horizontal line there are also 4 points: C(4, 2) = 6 triangles.
Exam tip: For n lines from one apex (counting the two sides) cut by k horizontal lines (counting the base), the count is k × C(n, 2) = 2 × C(4, 2) here.

questions.text:
Statements: Some bolts are nuts. All nuts are screws.
Conclusions: I. Some bolts are screws. II. All screws are nuts.
Which conclusion(s) follow(s)?
solution: Concept: The bolts that are nuts lie inside the screws circle.
So some bolts are screws: I follows. "All nuts are screws" does not mean all screws are nuts: II does not follow.
Answer: only I.
Exam tip: Some + All (in that order) gives a "Some" conclusion; All + Some gives no definite conclusion.

questions.text: One of three suspects A, B and C broke a gauge. A says, "B did it." B says, "I did not do it." C says, "A did not do it." Exactly one of the three statements is true. Who broke the gauge?
solution: Concept: Try each suspect as the culprit and count the true statements.
If A did it: A's statement false, B's true, C's false → exactly one true ✓.
If B did it: A's true, B's false, C's true → two true ✗. If C did it: A's false, B's true, C's true → two true ✗.
So A broke the gauge.
Exam tip: With a small number of cases, test every case systematically instead of reasoning in circles.
